snapshot.title: UPSC Schemes 2: Economic & Infra
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ UPSC v12.0 Hook: PLI: Manufacturing. Gati Shakti: 7 Engines. e-NAM: Agri. BharatNet: Gram Panchayat. UMANG: E-Gov.

quick_notes.title: Digital India
quick_notes.detail: 9 pillars. India Stack (Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker). UMANG app. BharatNet (Broadband to Gram Panchayats).
quick_notes.explanation: Digital India is a government programme launched in 2015 to transform India into a digitally empowered society. It is built on nine pillars, which are major areas of focus like broadband, universal mobile access, and e-governance. One key part of Digital India is the India Stack, a set of open digital platforms: Aadhaar is a 12-digit biometric identity number for residents; UPI stands for Unified Payments Interface, which allows instant money transfers between bank accounts using a mobile phone; and DigiLocker is a cloud-based service to store and share digital versions of official documents. Another tool is the UMANG app, which stands for Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance, and it gives citizens access to hundreds of government services on a single smartphone app. BharatNet is a project that aims to connect every Gram Panchayat (village-level local government body) with high-speed broadband internet.

quick_notes.title: PLI (Production Linked Incentive)
quick_notes.detail: Boost manufacturing. Incentives on incremental sales. 14 sectors (Electronics, Pharma, Auto, etc).
quick_notes.explanation: PLI stands for Production Linked Incentive, which is a government scheme designed to boost manufacturing in India by giving companies extra money based on how much more they sell compared to a previous year. The scheme works by offering a financial reward, usually a percentage of the value of the additional sales, to companies that increase their production and sales of certain goods. This reward is called an incentive, and it is only paid on the "incremental sales," meaning the extra sales made beyond a fixed base year's sales. The scheme currently covers 14 specific sectors, including Electronics (like mobile phones), Pharmaceuticals (medicines), Automobiles (cars and auto parts), and others like textiles and food products. For example, a company that makes electronics and sells 100 crore rupees worth in 2023 and then 150 crore rupees in 2024 would get a cash incentive on the extra 50 crore rupees of sales. The goal is to make India a global manufacturing hub by encouraging companies to produce more goods within the country.

quick_notes.title: PM Gati Shakti
quick_notes.detail: National Master Plan for Multi-modal connectivity. 7 engines (Roads, Railways, Airports, etc). Integration of 16 ministries.
quick_notes.explanation: PM Gati Shakti is a National Master Plan, which means it is a big government plan for the whole country, designed to connect different types of transport, called multi-modal connectivity, so that goods and people can move smoothly using roads, trains, and planes together. The plan is powered by 7 engines, which are the main areas of development: Roads, Railways, Airports, Ports, Mass Transport (like city buses and metro trains), Waterways (rivers and canals), and Logistics Infrastructure (warehouses and freight stations). To make this work, the plan integrates, or brings together, 16 different ministries, such as the Ministry of Road Transport and the Ministry of Railways, so they all share data and coordinate their projects on a single digital map. This integration helps avoid delays and wasted money by ensuring that, for example, a new road is built at the same time as a new railway line, instead of one being finished years before the other. The goal of PM Gati Shakti is to reduce the time it takes to move goods across the country, lower costs for businesses, and create more jobs by making India's infrastructure more efficient.

quick_notes.title: PMGSY
quick_notes.detail: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana. All-weather roads to unconnected habitations. Funding : Central (60:40).
quick_notes.explanation: PMGSY stands for Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, which is Hindi for Prime Minister's Rural Road Scheme. This is a government programme that builds all-weather roads, meaning roads that remain usable in rain or shine, to connect unconnected habitations, which are villages or settlements that currently have no road link to the outside. The funding for this scheme is shared between the central government and the state governments in a 60:40 ratio, so the central government pays 60 percent of the cost and the state government pays the remaining 40 percent.

quick_notes.title: e-NAM
quick_notes.detail: National Agriculture Market. Electronic trading portal for agri-commodities. Transparency in price discovery.
quick_notes.explanation: e-NAM stands for the electronic National Agriculture Market. It is an online trading platform created by the Government of India to connect different physical agricultural markets, called mandis, across the country. The system allows farmers to sell their agricultural products, like grains and vegetables, to buyers from any location, not just their local market. This helps farmers get a better price because they can see the prices offered in many mandis at once, a process called transparent price discovery. The platform is voluntary for states to join, and it aims to reduce the number of middlemen and make the entire buying and selling process more fair and efficient.
